ideas.hypothesis: Appraising transportation projects with social return on investment, which monetizes health, safety and social-inclusion outcomes, changes the priority ranking of candidate projects compared with conventional business-cost-saving appraisal, favoring projects that serve deprived areas.
ideas.test: Take 10-20 proposed projects from one regional transport agency's programme; compute standard benefit-cost ratios and SROI ratios using the same demand forecasts plus monetized social outcomes; compare rank correlations and check whether reranking favors deprived catchments.
ideas.disconfirming: SROI and conventional rankings are nearly identical (rank correlation above 0.9), or reranking does not favor deprived areas.

ideas.hypothesis: Upgrades to regional railway infrastructure reduce the income gap between peripheral and core districts, with effects concentrated in districts within commuting distance of the upgraded lines.
ideas.test: Difference-in-differences on German districts (Kreise) 1995-2015, comparing districts on upgraded regional lines with matched districts on unchanged lines; outcomes are GDP per capita and employment relative to the state average.
ideas.disconfirming: Treated peripheral districts show no convergence relative to controls, or diverge further.

ideas.hypothesis: Adding regional equity constraints to stochastic highway project selection models reduces projected regional development imbalance at a small cost in network-wide performance.
ideas.test: Re-run a published stochastic optimization project-selection model on a state highway programme with and without a constraint on the spread of investment per capita across regions; compare system performance and a regional disparity index of expected benefits.
ideas.disconfirming: Equity constraints cause large losses in system performance (e.g., more than 10%) or do not reduce benefit disparities.

ideas.hypothesis: Adding spatial accessibility indicators (to jobs, food and services) to integral evaluations of regional development efficiency improves their ability to predict future regional population and income growth.
ideas.test: For Ukrainian or other regions, construct the integral efficiency index with and without floating-catchment accessibility measures; compare out-of-sample prediction of five-year growth.
ideas.disconfirming: Accessibility-augmented indices predict growth no better than the original index.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions where local-loop unbundling at cost-based network element prices brought more competitive entry saw faster broadband adoption and faster growth in knowledge-intensive employment.
ideas.test: US county or EU regional panel 1998-2012: relate number of competitive local exchange carriers or unbundled lines to broadband penetration and sectoral employment growth, using variation in state unbundling price rulings.
ideas.disconfirming: Entry under unbundling is unrelated to broadband adoption or regional employment growth.

ideas.hypothesis: Economic zones with higher livability scores retain a larger share of the talent they develop or attract, lowering talent outflow.
ideas.test: City-level panel in the Economic Zone on the West Side of the Straits and comparison zones: regress net migration of university graduates on livability indicators (housing cost, green space, commute times), with city fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Livability has no association with graduate retention.

ideas.hypothesis: Residents of compact, mixed-use neighbourhoods purchase a higher share of fresh food than residents of dispersed areas with similar socioeconomic deprivation.
ideas.test: Link household food-purchase survey data to neighbourhood density and land-use mix in New Zealand urban areas, controlling for deprivation index and income.
ideas.disconfirming: Fresh food share does not vary with urban form after controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Randomly allocated innovation vouchers or R&D grants to small firms raise the probability of introducing new products within two years relative to unsuccessful applicants.
ideas.test: A lottery among eligible applicants to a state innovation-support programme (e.g., in Tasmania), followed by an innovation census survey of winners and losers after two years.
ideas.disconfirming: Winners and losers show no significant difference in new-product introduction.

ideas.hypothesis: Public R&D support agencies that use effectuation-informed due diligence select start-ups with higher survival and innovation rates than agencies using predictive business-plan assessment.
ideas.test: Compare cohorts of funded start-ups under two assessment protocols (before and after a protocol change in one agency) on three-year survival and patent or new-product outcomes.
ideas.disconfirming: Survival and innovation outcomes do not differ between assessment protocols.

ideas.hypothesis: Cities with greater related industrial variety urbanize and grow faster than cities with similar initial income but specialized structures, consistent with evolutionary mechanisms rather than pure capital accumulation.
ideas.test: Chinese prefecture-level panel 2000-2015: regress urban population growth and GDP growth on entropy-based related and unrelated variety measures from industrial census data.
ideas.disconfirming: Related variety does not predict urbanization or growth after controlling for capital and initial income.

ideas.hypothesis: Industrial relocation to the interior during the Second Sino-Japanese War left persistent effects, so that interior counties receiving relocated factories had higher industrial output shares decades later.
ideas.test: Historical county data on wartime factory relocations in the Northwest and Southwest linked to 1980s and 2000s county industrial output, comparing with neighbouring non-recipient counties.
ideas.disconfirming: Recipient counties show no persistent industrial advantage.

ideas.hypothesis: EU countries with higher pollution tax shares do not lose national competitiveness and gain in technological readiness scores, consistent with the Porter hypothesis.
ideas.test: EU-28 panel 2005-2018: regress Global Competitiveness Index pillars on lagged pollution tax revenue shares, with country and year fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Higher pollution tax shares predict lower competitiveness scores.

ideas.hypothesis: In developing countries, infrastructure quality mediates a large share of the link between economic development and social well-being indices.
ideas.test: Cross-section of ~100 developing countries: path analysis with GDP per capita, infrastructure index and social well-being index, estimating the indirect effect through infrastructure.
ideas.disconfirming: The indirect effect through infrastructure is small or insignificant.

ideas.hypothesis: Track access charges set on forward-looking incremental cost principles attract more entrant regional rail operators and raise patronage compared with charges set on historical costs.
ideas.test: European country panel after infrastructure-operations separation: relate access charge methodology to entrant market share and regional rail passenger-kilometres.
ideas.disconfirming: Access charge methodology has no relation with entry or patronage.

ideas.hypothesis: Incorporating smart-growth land-use effects into travel demand forecasts materially lowers estimated economic development impacts of highway capacity projects relative to transit projects.
ideas.test: For a sample of proposed projects in one metropolitan region, run the regional model with and without smart-growth adjustments and feed outputs into the same economic impact model; compare estimated impacts.
ideas.disconfirming: Estimated impacts change by less than a few percent.

ideas.hypothesis: Walkable new-community design raises residents' physical activity more in socioeconomically deprived growth areas than in affluent ones.
ideas.test: Longitudinal resident survey with accelerometers in several new housing developments differing in design and area deprivation, before and after moving.
ideas.disconfirming: The design effect on physical activity is equal or smaller in deprived areas.

ideas.hypothesis: Shared-space street redesigns increase residents' and visitors' social connectedness (incidental interactions, familiarity with neighbours) relative to conventional street layouts.
ideas.test: Before-after observation and survey study on one shared-space scheme and a comparable control street, counting stationary activities and social interactions.
ideas.disconfirming: No increase in social interactions or connectedness relative to the control street.

ideas.hypothesis: Higher land-use mix reduces severe pedestrian injury rates per walking trip because vehicle speeds fall in mixed-use areas.
ideas.test: Census-tract analysis of police crash data and travel survey walking trips in a metropolitan region, regressing injury rates on land-use mix entropy, controlling for traffic volume.
ideas.disconfirming: Injury rates per walking trip are unrelated or rise with land-use mix.

ideas.hypothesis: Growth of the financial (virtual) economy concentrates income gains in core regions and widens regional economic disparities.
ideas.test: Provincial panel (China or Ukraine) 2000-2018: regress regional income dispersion on financial-sector value-added share, with lagged values and region fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Financial-sector growth is associated with convergence or no change in disparities.

ideas.hypothesis: Rural road upgrades raise agricultural output and market participation most in territories far from regional centres.
ideas.test: District panel combining road construction records with agricultural output and marketed share, using staggered timing of upgrades.
ideas.disconfirming: No effect of road upgrades, or no gradient with distance to centres.

ideas.hypothesis: Hierarchical clustering of regions on multidimensional economic, social and ecological indicators produces groupings that predict subsequent growth better than single integral-index rankings.
ideas.test: Apply both methods to Ukrainian regional data for one base year; test whether cluster membership explains more variance in five-year growth than index quintiles.
ideas.disconfirming: Cluster membership explains no more growth variance than index-based groups.

ideas.hypothesis: Khaldunian institutional variables (justice, governance, accountability) explain variation in social well-being across Indonesian provinces beyond income and education.
ideas.test: Provincial cross-section: hierarchical regression of the human development or well-being index on economic factors, then add governance and justice indicators; test increment in explained variance.
ideas.disconfirming: Institutional variables add no significant explanatory power.

ideas.hypothesis: Augmenting a neoclassical growth model with urbanization as a productivity shifter significantly improves the explanation of provincial growth in China.
ideas.test: Provincial panel growth regressions 1990-2015 with and without urbanization rates, instrumenting urbanization with historical hukou reforms.
ideas.disconfirming: Urbanization adds no explanatory power once capital and labor are included.

ideas.hypothesis: Regional development programmes evaluated with SROI show higher social returns for social-infrastructure components than for firm-subsidy components.
ideas.test: SROI analysis of two to four components of one regional development programme using administrative and beneficiary survey data.
ideas.disconfirming: Firm-subsidy components show equal or higher SROI.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with higher shares of knowledge-intensive industries have higher start-up survival rates because of local knowledge spillovers.
ideas.test: Business register data for Australian regions: hazard models of start-up survival on regional knowledge-intensive employment share.
ideas.disconfirming: Start-up survival is unrelated to the knowledge-intensive industry share.

ideas.hypothesis: Economies that transitioned from planned to market systems saw faster declines in railway route length and rail freight share than comparable market economies.
ideas.test: Country panel 1990-2010 for transition and Western European economies: compare trends in rail network length and modal share.
ideas.disconfirming: Transition economies show no faster decline in rail infrastructure.

ideas.hypothesis: Transport schemes designed with structured community participation produce fewer post-opening accessibility complaints from disabled and elderly users.
ideas.test: Compare 20-30 street-design projects in one city by participation intensity, using complaint records and user surveys after opening.
ideas.disconfirming: Participation intensity is unrelated to accessibility complaints.

ideas.hypothesis: Port capacity expansion in coastal cities raises foreign-invested enterprise entry and improves their ratings of the local economic development environment.
ideas.test: Panel of Chinese coastal prefectures 2000-2015: relate port throughput capacity expansions to foreign-invested enterprise counts, using factor-analysis-based environment scores from enterprise surveys.
ideas.disconfirming: Port expansion does not precede higher foreign firm entry.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with more university-industry collaboration agreements show faster growth in innovation output per capita.
ideas.test: Regional panel of joint patents and collaboration contracts linked to patent and new-product output, with region fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Collaboration intensity does not predict innovation output.

ideas.hypothesis: Factor-analysis-derived weights for competitiveness indicators predict subsequent GDP growth better than the fixed weights of standard competitiveness indices.
ideas.test: Use Global Competitiveness Index sub-indicators for ~130 countries; build a factor-analytic index and compare its out-of-sample prediction of five-year growth with the official index.
ideas.disconfirming: The factor-analytic index predicts growth no better than official weights.
